failing_checks.note: Timber poles down both pavements with dozens of spans criss-crossing the carriageway. A single pole would be fine; this roofs the street over.

fix: Regenerate with buried services. At most one pole with a single service drop to one house.

failing_checks.note: Bright direct sun with hard shadows. Legitimate for a British summer day, so a soft detractor only. The ground is not bleached and the planting is green.

note: This fixture changed the rubric. An earlier version treated any hard blue-sky sun as a strong tell capping uk_score at 6, which would have rejected a real British summer street. The single pole on the right is also correctly ignored now.

note: Base score 7: rendered terraces with no distinctive architecture and nothing identifying in the built form. Eight confirmers lift it to 8. This is the confirmer rule doing the work.

A regional edge case, kept deliberately. This was generated as a failure fixture for timber cladding, but white weatherboard is genuine Kent, Essex, and Sussex vernacular, and the roof is plain tile over a brick chimney rather than asphalt shingle. A rubric that read timber cladding as automatically American would wrongly reject a real British house. Compare with 08, which is the actual American form.
